# Lucy

## Overview

- **Age:** 11 years old in Volume 1  <sub>[v1 c2 P62](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0062), [v1 c15 P1](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0001)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v1 c2 P62](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0062)</sub>
- **Origin:** Brierley (Pear Hill)  <sub>[v1 c2 P60](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0060), [v1 c2 P62](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0062)</sub>
- **Role:** Schoolgirl  <sub>[v1 c8 P37](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0037), [v1 c15 P8](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0008)</sub>

## Appearance

Isolde is an extremely lovely young girl with rosy cheeks, dark eyes, and shiny black hair. She is described as being slightly plumper than her closest friend, Nell, and she possesses expressive soulful eyes along with charming dimples.

_Sources: [v1 c8 P40](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0040), [v1 c12 P21](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0021), [v1 c12 P40](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0040), [v1 c21 P9](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0009)_

## Personality

Isolde is cheerful, pragmatic, and friendly, with a frequent laugh. Though she lacks Nell's intense imagination and loquacity, she is easily drawn into imaginative games and pledges of dramatic loyalty. She is deeply devoted to her friends, though she respects her mother's strict authority.

_Sources: [v1 c12 P26](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0026), [v1 c12 P36](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0036), [v1 c12 P37](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0037), [v1 c15 P1](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0001), [v1 c15 P30](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0030), [v1 c17 P5](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0005)_

## Traits

- Cheerful and prone to laughter  <sub>[v1 c12 P21](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0021), [v1 c12 P26](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0026)</sub>
- Pragmatic  <sub>[v1 c15 P1](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0001)</sub>
- Loyal companion  <sub>[v1 c12 P35](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0035), [v1 c17 P5](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0005)</sub>
- Afraid of swearing  <sub>[v1 c12 P30](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0030)</sub>
- Fear of crossing bridges  <sub>[v1 c2 P65](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0065)</sub>

## Abilities

- Singing ('Nelly in the Hazel Dell')  <sub>[v1 c12 P40](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0040)</sub>
- Crochet and handiwork  <sub>[v1 c17 P29](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0029), [v1 c18 P49](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0049)</sub>

## Goals

- To be the dearest and lifelong companion of Nell Harcourt  <sub>[v1 c12 P28](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0028), [v1 c12 P35](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0035), [v1 c17 P5](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0005)</sub>

## History

Isolde lives at Pear Hill in Brierley. After returning from a visit to her aunt in Delford, she meets Nell Harcourt and the two quickly swear a solemn vow of lifelong friendship over an imaginary stream. She and Nell share a playhouse called Larkrise and participate in numerous imaginative adventures. When her mother mistakenly believes Nell intentionally got Isolde intoxicated on homemade currant wine (which Nell had mistaken for raspberry cordial), Isolde is forbidden from playing with Nell, leading to a dramatic farewell. However, after Nell saves Isolde's younger sister Posy Fay from croup during a winter emergency, Mrs. Pembroke pardons Nell and allows the girls to resume their bosom friendship. Isolde later attends the local Brierley school alongside Nell, partakes in schoolhouse dramas, Sunday-school picnics, and community events, and ultimately becomes engaged to Gideon Duckett.

_Sources: [v1 c8 P37](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0037), [v1 c12 P23](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0023), [v1 c12 P35](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0035), [v1 c13 P13](../source/v01-c13.md#nw-v01-c13-p0013), [v1 c16 P22](../source/v01-c16.md#nw-v01-c16-p0022), [v1 c16 P42](../source/v01-c16.md#nw-v01-c16-p0042), [v1 c17 P3](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0003), [v1 c18 P21](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0021), [v1 c18 P43](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0043), [v1 c26 P2](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0002), [v1 c37 P0](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0000)_

## Background by volume

- Daughter of Mr. and Mrs. Pembroke of Pear Hill in Brierley  <sub>[v1 c2 P60](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0060), [v1 c2 P62](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0062), [v1 c12 P21](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0021)</sub>
- Named Isolde by a schoolmaster who lodged with her family when she was born  <sub>[v1 c2 P64](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0064)</sub>
- Has no sisters close to her age to play with  <sub>[v1 c12 P27](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0027)</sub>

## Quotes

> Well, I suppose that’s true. I am so happy that you have moved to Grey Shutters. Having a companion to play with will be wonderful.  <sub>[v1 c12 P27](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0027)</sub>

> The act of swearing is remarkably evil, after all.  <sub>[v1 c12 P30](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0030)</sub>

> Most certainly I shall, and no other intimate friend will ever be mine—it is not my desire to possess one. Loving anyone else as deeply as I love you is impossible for me.  <sub>[v1 c17 P5](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0005)</sub>

> You can be certain that my love for you, Nell, is devoted and will last forever.  <sub>[v1 c17 P9](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0009)</sub>
